newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index surge 6.52 percent.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index surge 6.52 percent.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index soared 6.52 percent in active trading on Tuesday due to institutional buying on rumours of measures to boost the market, brokers said.
The B share index rose 6.30 points to 102.86 after late profit-taking pushed it off its intraday high of 104.10. Turnover rose to HK$81.2 million from Monday's HK$58.35 million.
The strong rally of the B market was based on rumours that securities regulators were considering market-boosting measures after a long slump, brokers said.
"Sentiment looked bullish and speculative and institutions were the main traders," a broker at China Southern Securities said. The trend should extend into later this week, he added.
But, because the index has risen sharply over the past few sessions, profit-taking looms, one analyst said.
Trading focussed on large-cap issues, brokers said.

Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 8.44 million shares and rose HK$0.16 to HK$2.06, up from its recent offer price of HK$1.89. Dadonghai gained HK$0.25 to HK$1.80, with 5.91 million shares changing hands.

Motorcycle producer North Jianshe climbed HK$0.13 to HK$2.43 on trade of 1.98 million shares. Health Mineral Water, the sharpest gainer, surged HK$0.58, or 26.73 percent, to HK$2.75 on volume of 345,161 shares on speculative demand, brokers said.
Tellus Machinery followed suit, soaring HK$0.37, or 19.68 percent, to HK$2.25, with 123,800 shares traded.
China Vanke became the sole loser on speculative selling, brokers said. The property issue edged down HK$0.28, or 4.68 percent, to HK$5.70 in thin trade of 7,000 shares.

The A market continued to advance on Tuesday, due largely to institutional speculative buying of recently listed issues, but investors are turning cautious after the A index has repeatedly hit record highs, brokers said.
The A share index rose 9.75 points, or 2.23 percent, to close at a record high of 447.00, but turnover fell to 16.62 billion yuan from 18.20 billion yuan in the previous session.
The composite index put on 9.61 points, or 2.37 percent, to 415.79.
Tourist agency Zhangjiajie was the star, soaring 3.40 yuan, or 18.38 percent, to 21.90 yuan.
